assemblies.name: Front end: radiator support and cooling

out.name: Front Grille
out.reason: The grille clips into or beside the bumper cover; a cracked or pushed-in cover often breaks its tabs or mesh.

out.name: Fog Lamp
out.reason: Fog lamps sit in the bumper cover; a crack or dent next to one can break the lamp or its bracket.

out.name: Front Number Plate
out.reason: Plate and holder are fixed to the cover; a dent or crack at the plate usually bends or cracks them.

out.name: Front Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: The bumper end fixes to the front of the arch liner; a cracked or torn bumper end often tears the liner edge.

out.name: Front Bumper Beam
out.reason: Sits behind the cover and foam absorber; a pushed-in cover can bend it. Check with the bumper off.

out.name: Engine Undercover
out.reason: The undercover is fixed to the bumper's lower edge; a pushed-in or torn lower bumper can tear it or pull it down.

out.name: Headlamp
out.reason: The bumper corner meets the headlamp; a pushed-in or shifted corner can crack the lamp or snap its hidden mounting tabs.

out.name: Air Conditioning Condenser
out.reason: The first cooling part behind the bumper and grille; a pushed-in front can bend its fins or crack its pipes.

out.name: Radiator
out.reason: Sits behind the condenser; a deep frontal push can bend its core or crack its tanks. Coolant on the ground is the sign.

out.name: Front Subframe
out.reason: A crumpling frontal hit runs from the beam into the rails and subframe; it needs measuring once parts are off.

out.name: Steering Assembly
out.reason: The steering rack sits on the front subframe; a crush hit that moves the subframe can bend the rack or tie rods.

out.name: Suspension - Front
out.reason: A crush hit at a corner can push a front wheel back and bend arms or a strut; a wheel set back or turned is the sign.

out.name: Airbag System
out.reason: A hard frontal hit can fire the front airbags and lock the belt pretensioners; check cabin photos for a deployed bag.

out.name: Air Conditioning Condenser
out.reason: Sits right behind the grille; a grille pushed in, not just scratched, often dents the condenser fins or pipes.

out.name: Radiator
out.reason: Sits behind the grille and condenser; check it when the grille is pushed in or the bonnet front edge is dented.

out.name: Front Windscreen
out.reason: A bonnet folded back toward the cabin can hit the windscreen base and cowl; look for cracks along the lower edge.

out.name: Front Bumper Beam
out.reason: A headlamp broken with the bumper corner pushed in means the beam end below it may have taken the load too.

out.name: Front Wheel Arch Trim
out.reason: The arch trim clips onto the fender's arch lip; a dent there often cracks it or breaks its clips.

out.name: Front Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: The liner is fixed inside the fender's arch; a dent near the arch often tears it or leaves it hanging.

out.name: Headlamp
out.reason: The fender's front edge holds the headlamp's side; a fender pushed back can crack the lamp or its mounting tabs.

out.name: Suspension - Front
out.reason: A hit at the front corner can push the wheel back and bend an arm or the strut; a wheel set back or turned is the sign.

out.name: Steering Assembly
out.reason: A wheel pushed back at the corner can bend the tie rod or rack; a turned wheel or off-centre steering is the sign.

out.name: Front Subframe
out.reason: A crush hit at the front corner can move the subframe corner; it needs measuring with parts off.

out.name: Underbody / Chassis
out.reason: Behind the fender sit the inner apron and the front rail; a crumpled fender can mean they are bent too.

out.name: Wing Mirror
out.reason: The mirror is mounted at the door's front corner; a dent there can crack the housing or loosen the mount.

out.name: Front Door Glass
out.reason: A door pushed in, or with its frame twisted, can crack the glass or push it out of its run.

out.name: Front Window Regulator
out.reason: The regulator sits inside the door; a deep dent in the lower half, a torn skin or stuck glass means it may be bent.

out.name: Interior Trim
out.reason: The door trim card on the inside cracks or loses its clips when the door is pushed in.

out.name: Sill / Rocker Panel
out.reason: Load from a door pushed in at the bottom goes into the sill; a crease along the sill below the door is the sign.

out.name: Airbag System
out.reason: A door pushed into the cabin can fire the side or curtain airbag; check cabin photos for a deployed bag.

out.name: Rear Door Glass
out.reason: A door pushed in, or with its frame twisted, can crack the glass or push it out of its run.

out.name: Rear Window Regulator
out.reason: The regulator sits inside the door; a deep dent in the lower half, a torn skin or stuck glass means it may be bent.

out.name: Interior Trim
out.reason: The door trim card on the inside cracks or loses its clips when the door is pushed in.

out.name: Sill / Rocker Panel
out.reason: Load from a door pushed in at the bottom goes into the sill; a crease along the sill below the door is the sign.

out.name: Airbag System
out.reason: A door pushed into the cabin can fire the side or curtain airbag; check cabin photos for a deployed bag.

out.name: Front Window Regulator
out.reason: The glass rides on the regulator inside the door; glass stuck, out of its run or pushed in usually means a bent regulator.

out.name: Rear Window Regulator
out.reason: The glass rides on the regulator inside the door; glass stuck, out of its run or pushed in usually means a bent regulator.

out.name: Rear Number Plate
out.reason: Plate and holder sit on the bumper or just above it; a dent or crack at the plate usually bends or cracks them.

out.name: Rear Bumper Reflector
out.reason: Reflectors sit in the bumper ends; a crack or dent at that corner often breaks the reflector or its clips.

out.name: Parking Sensor
out.reason: Sensors sit in holes in the cover; a dent or crack near them can push them in, break the holders or cut the wiring.

out.name: Reversing Camera
out.reason: Where the camera sits in the bumper or the garnish just above it, a bumper pushed up or in can crack or misalign it.

out.name: Rear Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: The bumper end fixes to the rear arch liner; a cracked or torn bumper end often tears the liner edge.

out.name: Rear Bumper Beam
out.reason: Sits behind the cover and absorber; a pushed-in cover or an uneven boot-to-bumper gap can mean it is bent.

out.name: Rear End Panel
out.reason: The panel under the boot opening, behind the bumper; an uneven boot gap or a buckle under the boot sill is the sign.

out.name: Tail Lamp
out.reason: The bumper corner sits under the tail lamp; a corner pushed up, in or shifted can crack the lens or the housing.

out.name: Boot Floor Board
out.reason: A rear panel pushed forward can lift, bend or crack the boot floor board; it is seen with the boot open.

out.name: Boot Side Trim
out.reason: Boot side trims line the inside of the rear corners; a pushed-in corner can crack them or break their clips.

out.name: Exhaust System
out.reason: The tailpipe ends at the bumper; a pushed-in bumper can bend the pipe or break its hangers.

out.name: Rear Floor Panel
out.reason: A crush hit runs through the rear rails into the spare wheel well and floor; wrinkles show under the boot carpet.

out.name: Suspension - Rear
out.reason: A crush hit at a rear corner can push the wheel and bend an arm or the axle; a wheel turned or set back is the sign.

out.name: Fuel Tank
out.reason: The tank sits ahead of the rear floor; a deep rear crush can dent it or its filler pipe. Fuel on the ground is the sign.

out.name: Boot Lid Lamp
out.reason: Lamps mounted on the lid crack or come loose when the lid is dented or pushed in next to them.

out.name: Reversing Camera
out.reason: On many cars the camera sits in the lid's garnish above the plate; a dent there can crack or misalign it.

out.name: Rear Windscreen
out.reason: On a tailgate or hatch the rear glass sits in the lid, so a twisted lid can crack it. Not on a sedan's boot lid.

out.name: Boot Lid Lock
out.reason: The lock sits in the lid's lower edge; a buckled lid, or one that will not open or latch, usually means a bent lock.

out.name: Boot Lid Hinge
out.reason: A lid pushed forward or out of line bends its hinges; uneven gaps at the lid's top corners are the sign.

out.name: Boot Lid Weatherstrip
out.reason: The seal round the boot opening is cut or pushed out of place when the lid or the panel under it buckles.

out.name: Boot Lid Inner Trim
out.reason: The trim or insulator on the inside of the lid cracks or loses its clips when the lid is buckled or pushed in.

out.name: Rear End Panel
out.reason: The lid closes onto the rear end panel; a lid pushed in, or hitting on closing, often means that panel buckled too.

out.name: Rear Quarter Panel
out.reason: The lamp sits in an opening in the quarter; a pushed-in lamp can wrinkle that opening, often seen only with the lamp out.

out.name: Boot Lid Lamp
out.reason: The lid lamp sits right beside the tail lamp; a hit that cracks or pushes in one often reaches the other.

out.name: Tail Lamp
out.reason: The tail lamp sits in the quarter; a dent at the lamp opening often cracks the lamp or breaks its mounts.

out.name: Rear Wheel Arch Trim
out.reason: The arch trim clips onto the quarter's arch lip; a dent there often cracks it or breaks its clips.

out.name: Rear Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: The liner is fixed inside the quarter's arch; a dent near the arch often tears it or leaves it hanging.

out.name: Boot Side Trim
out.reason: The boot side trim lines the inside of the quarter; a pushed-in quarter cracks it or breaks its clips.

out.name: Rear End Panel
out.reason: The quarter's rear end joins the rear end panel; a quarter pushed in at the back can buckle it.

out.name: Suspension - Rear
out.reason: A hit at the rear corner can push the wheel in and bend an arm or the axle; a wheel turned or rubbing is the sign.

out.name: Rear Floor Panel
out.reason: A crumpled quarter can carry the load into the boot floor and spare wheel well; floor wrinkles are the sign.

out.name: Rear Subframe
out.reason: A crush hit at the rear corner can move the rear subframe; it needs measuring with parts off.

out.name: Sill / Rocker Panel
out.reason: The quarter's lower front edge meets the sill behind the rear door; a low hit there can crease the sill's rear end.

out.name: Boot Lid Weatherstrip
out.reason: The boot seal fits on this panel's top flange; a buckled panel cuts it or lifts it off.

out.name: Boot Lid Lock
out.reason: The lock's striker is on this panel; a panel pushed forward stops the lid latching or jams the lock.

out.name: Rear Floor Panel
out.reason: The rear end panel is welded to the boot floor; a panel pushed forward wrinkles the floor and spare wheel well behind it.

out.name: Front Tyre
out.reason: A rim dented or cracked at the lip can cut or bulge the tyre or lose its seal; check the sidewall next to the damage.

out.name: Front Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: A wheel struck hard enough to dent the rim can be pushed into the arch liner and tear it.

out.name: Suspension - Front
out.reason: A bent or cracked rim means the blow reached the hub; arms, strut and knuckle need checking, with an alignment.

out.name: Steering Assembly
out.reason: A front wheel struck hard enough to bend the rim can bend the tie rod; a turned wheel or off-centre steering is the sign.

out.name: Rear Tyre
out.reason: A rim dented or cracked at the lip can cut or bulge the tyre or lose its seal; check the sidewall next to the damage.

out.name: Rear Wheel Arch Liner
out.reason: A wheel struck hard enough to dent the rim can be pushed into the arch liner and tear it.

out.name: Suspension - Rear
out.reason: A bent or cracked rim means the blow reached the hub; arms or axle need checking, with an alignment.

out.name: Front Wheel
out.reason: A tyre cut or bulged by a kerb or pothole often comes with a dented or cracked rim lip at the same spot.

out.name: Rear Wheel
out.reason: A tyre cut or bulged by a kerb or pothole often comes with a dented or cracked rim lip at the same spot.

out.name: Exhaust System
out.reason: The exhaust hangs lowest under the car; scrape marks underneath usually reach the pipe, box or hangers too.

out.name: Fuel Tank
out.reason: The tank sits under the rear seat area; a hard strike underneath can dent it or its straps. Fuel on the ground is the sign.

out.name: Rear Subframe
out.reason: A hard strike under the rear can bend the rear subframe; it needs measuring with parts off.

out.name: Suspension - Rear
out.reason: A hard strike under the rear can bend arms or the axle; a rear wheel out of line is the sign.

out.name: Underbody / Chassis
out.reason: The sill joins the floor crossmembers; a sill crushed inward can bend the floor and crossmember behind it.

out.name: Steering Assembly
out.reason: The steering rack is bolted to the front subframe; a bent or moved subframe means the rack and tie rods need checking.

out.name: Suspension - Front
out.reason: The front lower arms mount on the subframe; a bent subframe usually means the arms and alignment need checking.

out.name: Suspension - Rear
out.reason: The rear arms mount on the rear subframe; a bent subframe usually means the arms and alignment need checking.

out.name: Front Subframe
out.reason: The front subframe sits just above the undercover; a cover torn by a kerb, hump or debris may mean it was struck too.

out.name: Steering Assembly
out.reason: The steering rack sits above the undercover; a hard strike from below can bend the rack or tie rods.

out.name: Radiator
out.reason: The radiator's lower edge sits above the front of the undercover; a torn front cover may mean it was hit.

out.name: Exhaust System
out.reason: The front exhaust pipe runs just behind and above the undercover; a dented or scraped cover often comes with a hit pipe.

out.name: Suspension - Front
out.reason: A strike that pushes the undercover up can reach the lower arms at its sides; a wheel out of line is the sign.

components.name: Front Bumper Absorber
components.note: The foam or plastic energy absorber between cover and beam; priced on its own once the bumper is off.

components.name: Front Bumper Bracket
components.note: The slide or retainer the cover's end clips into below the headlamp; a pushed or torn bumper end snaps it.

components.name: Front Parking Sensor
components.note: Today's Parking Sensor has no end, so a front bumper can't link it; the split lets the front one be named.

components.name: Fog Lamp Cover
components.note: The bezel or blank cover in the bumper's lower corners; it breaks with the cover even on cars with no fog lamp.

components.name: Radiator Support
components.note: The panel that carries the radiator, latch and headlamp inner mounts; a frontal push past the beam bends it.

components.name: Radiator Fan
components.note: Sits behind the radiator; a radiator pushed back cracks the shroud or blades.

components.name: Bonnet Hinge
components.note: A bonnet pushed back or folded bends its hinges; uneven bonnet-to-fender gaps at the rear corners are the sign.

components.name: Bonnet Latch
components.note: Bolted to the radiator support under the bonnet's front edge; a bonnet that will not shut or open points at it.

components.name: Bonnet Insulator
components.note: The pad clipped under the bonnet; renewed when the bonnet is buckled or replaced.

components.name: Front Door Lock
components.note: A door pushed in at its rear edge, or one that will not open or latch, usually has a bent lock.

components.name: Rear Door Lock
components.note: As the front door's: a jammed rear door or one pushed in at its rear edge.

components.name: Front Door Hinge
components.note: A hit at the door's front edge or a sagging door bends the hinges; a door that drops when opened is the sign.

components.name: Rear Door Hinge
components.note: As the front door's, on the centre pillar.

components.name: Front Door Handle
components.note: The outer handle sits in the skin; a dent or scrape across it often cracks or scratches it.

components.name: Rear Door Handle
components.note: As the front door's.

components.name: Rear Bumper Absorber
components.note: The energy absorber between the rear cover and beam.

components.name: Rear Bumper Bracket
components.note: The retainer the rear cover's end clips into under the tail lamp; a pushed or torn bumper end snaps it.

components.name: Rear Parking Sensor
components.note: The rear half of today's Parking Sensor, so the front and rear ones can be told apart.

components.name: Boot Lid Striker
components.note: The loop the lid's lock catches, on the panel under the opening; a panel pushed forward bends it.

components.name: Boot Lid Strut
components.note: The gas struts that hold a tailgate or lid up; a lid pushed out of line bends them. Some lids use torsion bars.

components.name: Rear Number Plate Lamp
components.note: Sits in the lid's garnish or the bumper above the plate; a hit at the plate cracks it.

components.name: Boot Lid Garnish
components.note: The trim strip across the lid that holds the plate lamps and often the camera.

components.name: Boot Lid Spoiler
components.note: The spoiler on the lid's top or rear edge; on many hatches it also holds the high-mount stop lamp.

components.name: Rear Wiper Motor
components.note: Inside a tailgate under the rear glass; a tailgate pushed in at its centre can crack it. Hatches and estates only.

components.name: High Mount Stop Lamp
components.stand_in: at the top of the boot lid or rear glass
components.note: On a tailgate's top edge or spoiler; a tailgate twisted or pushed in can crack it.

components.name: Fuel Filler Flap
components.note: The flap in one rear quarter; a dent across it bends the flap or its hinge. Which side is the car's own fact.
